title: Worker isolation Half B: route worker spawn through the dev container
description:
Follow-up to CAM-111 (Half A shipped in PR #110, v0.37.0), which added the additive isolation artifact: .devcontainer/{Dockerfile,devcontainer.json,init-firewall.sh} (non-root worker, pinned claude-code@2.1.197, egress default-deny with exactly 7 allowlisted domains) plus an exported-but-uncalled preflightWorkerContainer() helper and ADR 0003 + recovery-runbook section (x). Half B is the behavior-changing integration half Half A deliberately deferred.

Scope: (1) rewrite the worker spawn in src/supervisor/worker-argv.ts and host.ts to launch the implementer+reviewer worker INSIDE the container (devcontainer up/exec or docker run) attached to the tmux pane PTY, preserving spawn invariants: env -u CLAUDECODE (CAM-43), lowercase --session-id (CAM-23), atomic send-keys text+Enter (CAM-55). (2) Wire preflightWorkerContainer() into the dispatch path so a missing Docker daemon or unbuilt image is caught before dispatch. (3) FAIL-CLOSED: if the container does not start, the worker MUST NOT fall back to running un-contained on the host; the loop emits a clear error and halts/escalates (a silent host fallback defeats the gate). (4) Credentials: git push via a repo-scoped/short-lived GITHUB_TOKEN through containerEnv (never ~/.ssh or a host cred file); claude auth via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude setup-token) or the named ~/.claude volume; document the credential handling. (5) Live validation (issue acceptance criterion 10, requires:operator): a real/representative story completes GREEN inside the container (bun test + tsc + git push pass under the firewall), captured as evidence (ties into CAM-116). (6) Docs: extend the recovery-runbook container section with fail-closed behavior and container-failure recovery.

Gotchas: the whole-process firewall now governs the implementer Step-5.5 WebFetch doc-validation too (keep heavy doc reads at plan-time in the orchestrator, outside the container; worker WebFetch is best-effort within the allowlist, do not silently lose doc validation); Docker Desktop on macOS runs a Linux VM so the worker runs Linux while tmux stays on the host pane (attach by PTY); the reference init-firewall.sh resolves domains to IPs once at container start, so CDN-backed hosts (raw.githubusercontent.com, *.github.com) rotate IPs and can later-drop, needs periodic re-resolve or DNS-based matching (reviewer SUGGESTION, CAM-111 round 1); objects.github.com is not a real LFS host (LFS objects live at objects.githubusercontent.com), fix the *.github.com subdomain list if git LFS is needed.

After this ships it WIRES the spawn, so rebuild+reinstall+restart the sidecar to encarnate the new spawn behavior before relying on it (Half A needed no rebuild because it was inert). Depends on CAM-111 (shipped). Priority: safety net for full-autonomy (plan_approval=auto is live); per CAM-111 escalation rule (Fase 1 rises to P1 when plan_approval=auto is on) and because Half B is the actual enforcement, it is P1, above the plan/ship-runner epics.

spec.scope: Half B of CAM-111 (worker isolation): route the worker spawn through the dev container so the implementer/reviewer/planner/auditor workers run INSIDE the fail-closed, egress-firewalled container instead of un-contained on the host. CAM-111 Half A shipped the inert artifact (.devcontainer/{Dockerfile,devcontainer.json,init-firewall.sh}, non-root bun user, pinned claude-code@2.1.197, egress default-deny + 7-domain allowlist, NET_ADMIN/NET_RAW, workspace bind mount, named ~/.claude volume) + an exported-but-uncalled preflightWorkerContainer() helper + ADR 0003. Half B is the behavior-changing integration. Decisions from the grill: (Q1) invoke via RAW docker (docker build from the Dockerfile + one long-lived `docker run` + `docker exec -it <container> <shellCmd>` as the pane command; the host tmux pane is the controlling PTY), with a parity test asserting the TS docker-run args match devcontainer.json (no runtime JSONC parse, drift caught at test time). (Q2) ONE long-lived container per session, reused across dispatches via docker exec (mirrors the reused worker-pane; amortizes init-firewall; workspace is bind-mounted so repo state is shared regardless; mutex=1 worker keeps exec sequential); contain ALL FOUR worker types (implementer, reviewer, planner, auditor) via the single-location docker-exec wrap at loop.ts:733 + plan-runner.ts:268/294 (plan-argv.ts builders need no change). (Q3) git push authenticates via HTTPS + a fine-grained repo-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents:write on cam-cli only) injected via containerEnv, NEVER ~/.ssh / host cred file / the broad host gh token; operator-provisioned (documented setup). (Q4) claude authenticates via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude setup-token) injected via containerEnv (one credential model with the GITHUB_TOKEN); live-validation must confirm the interactive TUI worker reads it, with populate-the-named-~/.claude-volume as the documented fallback. (Q5) FAIL-CLOSED: preflightWorkerContainer() runs before EVERY dispatch + a runtime docker-exec-failure catch; on failure the worker NEVER falls back to the host, the loop escalates (existing escalateFn) + returns blocked with a clear reason (no dependency on CAM-151; the retry/abandon gate upgrade is a follow-up). (Q6) the firewall is rewritten to DNS-based matching (dnsmasq resolves the allowlisted domains and adds the resolved IPs dynamically) so CDN hosts (raw.githubusercontent.com, *.github.com) survive IP rotation over the long-lived container's lifetime with ZERO rotation window (frozen-IP dig-once drops legit git push/WebFetch mid-session); + fix objects.github.com -> objects.githubusercontent.com (the real LFS host). Depends on CAM-111 (shipped). Safety net for live full-autonomy (plan_approval=auto is on); P1, must land before CAM-139 (drainer) goes fully live.
acceptanceCriteria: All four worker spawns (implementer, reviewer, planner, auditor) launch INSIDE the container via `docker exec -it <container> env -u CLAUDECODE ... claude ...` wrapped at the dispatch sites (loop.ts + plan-runner.ts); the host tmux pane is the controlling PTY; the plan-argv.ts/worker-argv.ts builders are reused unchanged (wrap at the respawn-pane call site). [oracle: bun test]

The sidecar builds the image (docker build from .devcontainer/Dockerfile) and runs ONE long-lived container per session, reused across dispatches via docker exec; the docker-run args include the devcontainer.json runArgs/mounts (cap-add NET_ADMIN + NET_RAW, workspace bind mount, named ~/.claude volume, remoteUser bun, containerEnv). [oracle: bun test]

A parity test asserts the TS docker-run args match .devcontainer/devcontainer.json (cap-add, mounts, volume, containerEnv, remoteUser); any drift fails the test (CAM-49/68/79 parity idiom, no runtime JSONC parse). [oracle: bun test]

Spawn invariants preserved through the docker-exec wrap: env -u CLAUDECODE (CAM-43) runs INSIDE the container before claude, lowercase --session-id (CAM-23), atomic send-keys text+Enter to the host pane (CAM-55), mutex 1 worker-pane (CAM-55). [oracle: bun test]

preflightWorkerContainer() runs before EVERY worker dispatch (daemon-unreachable/image-missing/image-stale reasons); on not-ready the dispatch halts fail-closed before any host spawn. [oracle: bun test]

FAIL-CLOSED: if the container cannot start (preflight fail OR docker-exec runtime failure), the worker NEVER falls back to running un-contained on the host; the loop escalates via the existing escalateFn + returns a blocked terminal with a clear reason (e.g. 'container failed to start: <reason>; NOT falling back to host'). [oracle: bun test]

git push authenticates via HTTPS + a fine-grained repo-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents:write on the one repo) injected via containerEnv; NO ~/.ssh mount, NO host cred file, NOT the broad host gh token; the token is operator-provisioned via a documented setup step. [oracle: bun test + grep asserting no ssh mount]

claude authenticates via CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN injected via containerEnv (operator-provisioned via `claude setup-token`); the recovery-runbook documents populating the named ~/.claude volume as the fallback if the interactive TUI worker does not read the token. [oracle: bun test + file-assert]

The firewall (init-firewall.sh) uses DNS-based matching (dnsmasq resolving the allowlisted domains and adding resolved IPs dynamically) so CDN-backed allowlisted hosts (raw.githubusercontent.com, *.github.com) survive IP rotation over the long-lived container's lifetime with no frozen-IP drop; the 7-domain allowlist semantics are preserved and the self-verify (allowed host succeeds, non-allowed fails) still passes. [oracle: file-assert + operator smoke]
The LFS subdomain is corrected to objects.githubusercontent.com (objects.github.com is not a real LFS host). [oracle: grep]

Live validation (requires:operator, hand-filed): a representative story completes GREEN inside the container (bun test + tsc + git push all pass under the firewall) and claude auth works, captured as evidence (ties into CAM-116). [oracle: reviewer-judgment / operator]

Deterministic units tested with injectable spawnFn/probe: docker-exec wrap shape, preflight-before-every-dispatch gating, fail-closed escalate+blocked path, credential env threading (GITHUB_TOKEN + CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN via containerEnv), devcontainer.json parity. bun run check:all passes. [oracle: bun run check:all]

Docs: the recovery-runbook container section is extended with the fail-closed behavior, container-failure recovery, and the credential provisioning setup; an ADR (extend 0003 or add a new one) records the containerized-spawn + fail-closed-no-host-fallback decision. [oracle: file-assert]
gotchas: SPLIT AT PLAN TIME (jobSize-3; the enforcement is fairly atomic so watch the fault line; mirrors CAM-111/CAM-117): B-1 SUBSTRATE = docker build/run orchestration in TS + DNS-based firewall rewrite + credential plumbing (how GITHUB_TOKEN + CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN reach containerEnv, tested) + preflight wiring (container correct+authenticated+firewalled but workers still spawn on host). B-2 FLIP-SPAWN = docker-exec wrap the 4 dispatch sites + fail-closed no-host-fallback + live validation. File the deferred half as a stage:idea follow-up via /cam-issue BEFORE branching (keeps the CAM-121 guard clean).

REBUILD-GATE at B-2: routing the spawn through the container is a behavior change. After B-2 ships, rebuild+reinstall+restart the sidecar (rm -f ~/.local/bin/cam; bash scripts/build-release.sh --install; kill $(cat .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid); nohup cam sidecar >> .claude/cam-supervisor.log 2>&1 & echo $! > .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid; disown) BEFORE relying on containerized workers. The B-1 substrate is inert like Half A (no rebuild).

CONTAIN ALL FOUR workers (implementer/reviewer/planner/auditor): the docker-exec wrap is a single-location interception covering loop.ts:733 + plan-runner.ts:268/294; leaving planner/auditor un-contained is a hole in the gate. The plan-argv.ts and worker-argv.ts builders need NO change (they already emit env -u ... claude ... via workerEnvPrefix + shellEscape); wrap the string at the respawn-pane call sites.

ORDERING vs CAM-151: both touch plan-runner.ts (CAM-150 wraps the dispatch sites; CAM-151 wires runPlanPhase live). CAM-150 is P1 (safety net for live plan_approval=auto) and MUST land before CAM-139 (drainer) goes fully live: do not run the unattended drainer with workers outside the sandbox. Whoever lands last rebases.

The whole-process firewall now governs the worker's Step-5.5 WebFetch doc-validation too (only api.anthropic.com + the 7 allowlisted hosts reachable). Keep heavy doc reads at plan-time in the orchestrator (outside the container); worker WebFetch is best-effort within the allowlist, do NOT silently lose doc validation.

macOS Docker Desktop runs a Linux VM, so the worker runs Linux inside the container while tmux stays on the host pane; attach by PTY via docker exec -it (the host pane is the controlling terminal). env -u CLAUDECODE must run INSIDE the container (docker exec ... env -u ... claude), lowercase --session-id and atomic send-keys are unchanged (send-keys still targets the host pane).

CREDENTIALS are a NEW operator setup requirement (a precondition of the first containerized run): provision a fine-grained repo-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN (contents:write on cam-cli) + a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude setup-token), available to the sidecar (env var or a gitignored secret file) and injected via containerEnv. NEVER ~/.ssh mount, NEVER a host cred file, NEVER the broad host gh token (undercuts the least-privilege gate).

LIVE-VALIDATION (criterion 11) is an operator ceremony hand-filed as a requires:operator story (the subagent-planner does NOT emit requires:operator stories); the operator runs a representative story in the container, confirms green gates + working auth, and captures evidence (ties into CAM-116).

fail-closed reuses the EXISTING escalateFn + blocked-return (loop.ts:350/1162), NOT the CAM-151 generic operator-decision gate, so CAM-150 has no cross-dependency on CAM-151 and can ship independently as the P1 safety net; the retry/abandon gate upgrade is a follow-up once both land.
